Health: where the account stands today

Health = EWS_SCORE × 100. EWS is PagerDuty's pre-validated behavioral composite, read directly from the data source. It integrates six behavioral signals: seat deployment, active responders (90 days), escalation policies generating incidents each month, mobile notification reach, high-urgency incidents resolved by a human, and EP schedule coverage with incidents. No recomputation happens in this report.

Each account card shows three context panels that explain what is driving the EWS level. Adoption shows how broadly the product is deployed and configured. Engagement shows how actively teams are using the platform. Outcomes shows sentiment signals from customer communications. These panels are independent context, not inputs to the health score.

Green ≥ 50 Healthy behavioral signals Yellow 40–49.9 Below target, watch closely Red < 40 Low engagement, high risk

Momentum: which direction the account is heading

Momentum starts at zero and accumulates points from behavioral signals. The result is a label: Positive (≥ +2 pts), Stable (between −2 and +2), or Negative (≤ −2 pts). The Trajectory breakdown panel on each account's card lists only the signals with a nonzero contribution for that account, so the number of rows shown varies from account to account.

Deployment signals look at the 12-month OLS slope of seat deployment and the 3-month rolling window change, rewarding growth and penalising contraction. Incident volume uses OLS regression with a statistical significance gate (|t| ≥ 2) so noise does not score, plus an EWMA to confirm whether recent activity is above or below the account's own baseline. EWS trend signals fire when the EWS score itself is on a statistically significant sustained decline, or has been persistently in the Red tier for six or more consecutive months. Sentiment signals penalise low absolute sentiment and score the direction of change, so deterioration shows up even before hitting the low threshold. Pricing friction penalises active negative pricing language and escalates if it persists historically. ARR downgrades penalise a realized drop in billed ARR of more than $50K in a non-renewal month. This is a different signal from the ARR-at-risk flag described below: a downgrade reflects a change that has already happened in the account's billing history, while the ARR-at-risk flag is a forward-looking risk a CSM confirms directly in Salesforce, and the two do not always occur on the same accounts.

Competitive risk is the strongest signal in the model. When a competing tool is detected in a customer's environment at an active migration stage, it immediately forces a Negative momentum classification and a hard override to Needs Attention, overriding every other signal. This includes Competitor API Activity (Account-wide), which does not subtract points from Trajectory on its own, since Trajectory reflects only the account's own operational and billing signals, not competitor presence, but which still triggers this same override whenever it fires. A second, independent override works the same way for ARR: any account with a confirmed at-risk amount in Salesforce is routed to Needs Attention outright, regardless of Health or Momentum, and its Momentum is forced Negative alongside it. Both are treated as hard overrides because a competitor being installed, or a confirmed dollar figure already logged against the account, are among the clearest signals that a customer relationship needs attention even when the score still looks fine.

The combined result is a Positive, Stable or Negative trajectory label. Because some signals feed both dimensions, a customer in decline will show warning signs in both Health and Momentum. Momentum will surface them first, because it measures the rate of change before the current level has visibly deteriorated.

The four action groups

Expand: Green health (EWS ≥ 50), stable or positive momentum. The customer is realizing value and behavioral signals are not declining. Focus on growth: run expansion business reviews and introduce unconfigured capabilities.

Protect: Green health, negative momentum. The customer looks healthy today but key signals are moving in the wrong direction. Act now before the health score follows: freeze upsell motions and diagnose the root cause immediately.

Nurture: Yellow or Red health (EWS < 50), stable or positive momentum. Below target but not deteriorating. Run value reviews, close adoption gaps, and work to move them into Green.

Needs Attention: Below healthy with negative momentum, or at-risk due to routing overrides (health below 35; Red health with a raw Trajectory total of −1 or worse; a competitor detected by any one of the five equally weighted detection sources, at any migration stage; or a confirmed ARR-at-risk entry in Salesforce). Escalate to leadership, freeze all commercial motions, and put resources on removing whatever is blocking the customer.

Timing: how urgent is the action

Every account card shows a Timing chip that converts days to renewal into an urgency level. It sits alongside Health and Trajectory in the scores bar at the top of each card.

CRITICAL   0–180 days   Act nowMID-TERM   181–270 days   Plan and prepareLONG-TERM   271+ days   Monitor and build

Timing does not change which group an account belongs to - that is determined by Health and Momentum. It determines urgency within the group. A Needs Attention account at 30 days is a fire. The same account at 250 days is a serious problem with time to address it properly. Use Timing to sequence your week: Critical accounts in any group go first.

What to think when a customer is unhealthy

Always look at momentum first. An unhealthy customer with stable or positive momentum is a recovery in progress. They are in a difficult place but not getting worse, and the right support can move them up. An unhealthy customer with negative momentum requires immediate action: they are sliding and the window to act is closing. Health tells you the severity. Momentum tells you the direction. Timing tells you how many days you have. A competitor signal overrides all three and demands an immediate response regardless of everything else.

Health tiers (50 Green / 40 Yellow, re-tiered a second time on July 24, 2026: Green now merges the official EWS Yellow band (50-65) with the official Green band (65+), Yellow now corresponds to the official Orange band (40-50)) and momentum thresholds are calibrated against the Nov 2025–Jan 2026 churned account retrospective (503 accounts). The framework detected 80% of churned accounts before churn. The remaining 20% fall into three structural categories: insufficient history (≤4 months), genuinely healthy at churn (external drivers such as M&A or budget), and chronic low adoption with no behavioral decline. Thresholds should be re-validated as the cohort grows. The sentiment rescaling formula is (raw + 1) / 2 × 100, converting the raw −1 to +1 field to a 0–100 scale. API_WATCH_IN_CUSTOMER is a pre-computed field read as-is; no recomputation occurs. Health tier thresholds (Green ≥ 50, Yellow 40–49.9, Red < 40, re-tiered a second time on July 24, 2026: Green now spans the official EWS Yellow and Green bands combined) and momentum point values are calibrated against a retrospective of 503 churned accounts (Nov 2025–Jan 2026), achieving 80% pre-churn detection. Timing tiers (CRITICAL 0–180 / MID-TERM 181–270 / LONG-TERM 271+) follow the Customer Health Framework (slide 8). Timing does not affect group routing; it determines urgency within the group. All data comes exclusively from the PagerDuty customer data export. A confirmed ARR-at-risk entry in Salesforce forces an account to Needs Attention with Negative Momentum. The Sentiment level and Sentiment direction signals apply a −1.0 point penalty at their most negative tier.
The model has two independent dimensions scored separately then combined to route each account. All data comes exclusively from the PagerDuty customer behavioral data export.

Health = EWS_SCORE × 100. It is a single number read directly from the data source. EWS is PagerDuty's pre-validated behavioral composite; this report does not recompute it. Health answers: where does this account stand right now?

Momentum starts at zero and accumulates points from 11 independent signal groups. It answers: which direction is this account heading? Four of those signals are EWS time-series signals (they measure whether the EWS score itself is declining, dropping suddenly, or stuck in the Red tier). The remaining seven signal groups are completely independent of EWS: seat deployment velocity, incident volume trend, sentiment level, sentiment direction, pricing friction, ARR downgrades, and competitor presence. This means an account can have a stable EWS score but still show Negative momentum if, for example, sentiment is deteriorating or a competitor has been detected.

Timing converts days to renewal into an urgency tier. It does not affect group routing - that is determined by Health and Momentum alone. It answers: how soon does this account need attention? CRITICAL (0–180 days): act now. MID-TERM (181–270 days): plan and prepare. LONG-TERM (271+ days): monitor and build.

Health tiers: Green ≥ 50 Yellow 40–49.9 Red < 40

Routing overrides (independent of momentum, approved framework change July 29, 2026): Health < 35 forces NEEDS ATTENTION regardless of momentum (unchanged). Health < 40 AND momentum pts ≤ −1 also forces NEEDS ATTENTION (unchanged). Unified competitor override: if ANY of five independent sources fires - F_COMPETITOR_RISK = 1 (regardless of migration stage), API_WATCH_POINT_SOLUTION_12M_BOOLEAN = 1, API_WATCH_IN_CUSTOMER = 1, a qualifying CSM Notes detection (confidence ≥ 3 with a THREAT direction; a DISPLACING direction means PagerDuty is displacing the competitor and does not fire), or a Gong Calls replacement-risk score of 4 or 5 - the account is forced to NEEDS ATTENTION with NEGATIVE Momentum, full stop. No stage gating, no partial-strength case. ARR-at-risk override: a confirmed entry in the SFDC ARR-at-risk file forces NEEDS ATTENTION regardless of health or momentum, in any group - this replaces the prior Green-health-only PROTECT reroute. These overrides are independent of each other and of the P3/P4 health-momentum triggers above; the group is NEEDS ATTENTION if ANY of them fire, otherwise the standard health/trajectory matrix below applies.

Part 2: Momentum (trajectory)

Starts at 0. Eleven independent signals add or subtract points. Result: ≥ +2 → POSITIVE  |  ≤ −2 → NEGATIVE  |  else → STABLE. As of the July 29, 2026 framework change, a competitor signal from ANY of five independent sources (CSV migration risk, API Watch point-solution, API Watch (account-wide), a qualifying CSM Notes detection, or a Gong Calls replacement-risk score of 4-5) always overrides and forces NEGATIVE regardless of the raw point total, and also forces the group itself to NEEDS ATTENTION - not just an EXPAND block. A confirmed SFDC ARR-at-risk entry independently forces NEEDS ATTENTION regardless of health or momentum. Sentiment level and Sentiment direction apply a −1.0 point penalty at their most negative tier.

Part 3: Routing and priority
GroupConditionAction
EXPANDGreen health + POSITIVE or STABLE momentum + no competitor override + no confirmed ARR riskGrowth: unconfigured modules, expansions, QBRs
PROTECTGreen health + NEGATIVE momentum, with no competitor override and no confirmed ARR risk (both of those now route straight to NEEDS ATTENTION instead)Freeze upsell. Diagnose before score follows.
NURTUREYellow/Red health + POSITIVE or STABLE momentumClose adoption gaps. Move to Green.
NEEDS ATTENTIONYellow/Red health + NEGATIVE momentum, or any override conditionEscalate. Freeze commercial. Investigate immediately.

Routing triggers (approved framework change, July 29, 2026 - replaces the retired P1/P2/P5/P6/P7 strict-priority hierarchy and the retired four-tier competitor hierarchy; all of the following are independent, group is NEEDS ATTENTION if ANY fire, otherwise the standard health/trajectory matrix above applies):

  • Health < 35: forces NEEDS ATTENTION regardless of momentum direction (unchanged).
  • Health < 40 AND momentum pts ≤ −1 (raw points, not the trajectory label): forces NEEDS ATTENTION (unchanged).
  • Unified competitor override - ANY of five independent sources firing forces NEEDS ATTENTION + NEGATIVE trajectory, full stop, no stage gating and no partial-strength case: F_COMPETITOR_RISK = 1 regardless of migration stage (Product Intelligence Model), API_WATCH_POINT_SOLUTION_12M_BOOLEAN = 1 (Data Science Model), or API_WATCH_IN_CUSTOMER = 1 (Data Science Model and/or Product Intelligence Model, rolled up across every account sharing the same PagerDuty customer record), a qualifying CSM Notes detection at confidence ≥ 3 with direction THREAT, not COEXIST and not DISPLACING (CSM Notes/Salesforce), or a Gong Calls replacement_risk score of 4 or 5 (Gong Calls).
  • ARR-at-risk override - a confirmed entry in the SFDC ARR-at-risk file forces NEEDS ATTENTION regardless of health or momentum, in any group, and forces Momentum to NEGATIVE alongside it.
Part 3b: Timing (urgency within group)

Timing is the third dimension of the framework (slide 8 of the Customer Health Framework deck). It does not change group assignment - it determines urgency within the group, so CSMs can sequence their week correctly. Source field: TERM_END (days computed at render time).

Days to renewalTiming labelColorMeaning
0–180 daysCRITICALRedAct now. Renewal is this or next quarter. Any risk must be resolved immediately.
181–270 daysMID-TERMAmberPlan and prepare. Enough runway to intervene, but action must start now.
271+ daysLONG-TERMGreenMonitor and build. Use this time proactively - do not wait for problems to appear.

How Timing and Group interact (from framework slide 8): Green health + Positive momentum + Critical timing → EXPAND, High priority. Green health + Negative momentum + any timing → PROTECT, High priority (momentum risk is urgent regardless of runway). Needs Attention + Critical timing → escalate immediately, highest priority in the portfolio.
